A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpenGPT-4o-Image work. Their main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model fine-tuning experiments, data-scaling results, training-strategy comparisons and qualitative evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–8 and the qualitative comparisons in Figures 5–6.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same task taxonomy, structured prompt generation, GPT-4o-based data construction, reference-image procedure and multi-turn editing pipeline. Appendix C's quality-control procedure is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Training sources and generation/editing task coverage are unchanged, including the categories in Tables 9–10. Both versions evaluate on GenEval, DPG-Bench, GEdit-Bench and ImgEdit-Bench.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–5 and the ShareGPT-4o-Image comparison in Table 7. Correcting AnyEdit's citation in Section 2.3 and Table 1 does not change an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both versions report identical model configurations, benchmark metrics, 20K/30K/40K sampling experiments and separate-versus-unified training comparisons. No evaluation setting or protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The data-scaling analysis in Table 6, training-strategy comparison in Table 8 and qualitative cases in Figures 5–6 are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–8 and qualitative examples in Figures 5–6 are unchanged. For example, fine-tuned UniWorld-V1 remains at 3.86 on ImgEdit-Bench and Harmon at 0.86 on GenEval.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The descriptive task definitions and pipeline reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a hierarchical taxonomy, automated construction of 80K pairs across 11 domains and 51 subtasks, and improved generation/editing performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of dataset quality and model improvements remain unchanged, as do Appendix B.3's task-interference discussion and Section 5's limitations concerning GPT-4o biases and benchmark representativeness.

D1.justification: Data preparation, gpt-image-1 usage, reported model details and code/dataset access links are unchanged. No implementation, hyperparameter or hardware information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yu et al. (2025), AnyEdit: Mastering Unified High-Quality Image Editing for Any Idea, and cites it in Section 2.3 and Table 1 instead of Jiang et al.'s knowledge-editing paper. The broader research positioning is unchanged; Tables 2 and 5 still cite Jiang et al.

P1.justification: The title page renumbers the PKU and Kling Team affiliations and removes the displayed manuscript date. Apart from citation edits, the prose, terminology and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title-page header changes, and the additional reference causes limited reflow of bibliography and appendix text and table placement. Figures, table structures and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 partially corrects an attribution error by linking the AnyEdit discussion and dataset comparison to the relevant image-editing paper, improving scholarly accuracy and traceability. The gain is limited: Tables 2 and 5 retain the incorrect citation, while the methods, evidence, claims and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
